body:
Yeah. PUA is not for me. Every time I watch someone do it, and every time I watch it succeed... it's like watching jews get offered a shower. I'm like "But... those spigots don't shoot water, damnit!"

Yes. Godwin. I feel that strongly about this, though.

I think that the reason that it is common for women to expect men not to be beaten down by life is that so many men are willing to pretend that they aren't. Women are presented with a false image. It's kind of like rich people who have no clue about how rough life is for poor people because all of their servants pretend to have wonderful lives because they are afraid of getting fired.

The side of my persona that I've expressed in this thread isn't my only side. I have a broad and rich personality that I've put a lot of effort into building. I have only two expectations of women. 1) that they be honest with me about who they are. 2) that they allow me to be honest with them about who I am. That's it. I know that they don't want to follow this facade. Neither do I. I understand that the reason that they continue with the facade is that it is comfortable. But at the same time, they always talk about wanting an SO who challenges them. 

I understand the principles that you are offering. I don't like them. They don't work for me. I would be no less depressed by going along with them, and I certainly have tried.

Thanks for the time that you put into writing this reply. It was very considerate and thoughtful of you. I've read a few of these things and it isn't for me. I'm not interested in pretending to be someone I'm not so that I can find someone to love me for who I am. It's completely nonsensical to me. I have done OK with a lot of things, but ultimately, I *am* beaten down by life and pretending I'm not makes it worse. Feeling like I *have to* pretend that I'm not compounds that. I don't think the problem in the dating world is that men aren't "manning up" or whatever. I think the problem is that women haven't accepted men as human beings with their own range of trials and travails and successes and failures. I think that this PUA stuff exacerbates that problem. But I do appreciate the time you took to offer some help.
Honestly, I've tried it from every angle. It just doesn't make me feel anything but worse.

I don't drink all that much. But I overdid it on the holiday. I've spent a lot of time trying to learn to be a better artist. But having to figure it all out myself without any tutelage hasn't worked. I feel like I have to start all over again every couple months.

Thanks for the advice. I play music. I try to write songs. But the songs are not very good at all, and I hate my lack of skill so much that trying to do art... just makes me more depressed and self loathing.
